A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same PCoT study. All 25 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–H, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original persuasion-detection and disinformation-detection experiments, including prompting comparisons, ablations, and the BERT evaluation in Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main evaluation in Table 5 and the appendix analyses and BERT comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix F retain the same two-stage PCoT procedure: persuasion detection with explanations followed by disinformation classification. Inputs, outputs, components, and prompt templates are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use CoAID, ECTF, ISOT Fake News, MultiDis, and EUDisinfo for disinformation evaluation, plus SemEval 2023 for persuasion detection. Language, domain, article/post, and prior/post-cutoff coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: The same comparisons remain: VaN, Z-CoT, DeF-SpeC, RaR, CoVe, o1-mini, o3-mini, and BERT. The persuasion-detection prompt comparators in Section 4 and Appendix E are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sampling, evaluation metrics, zero-shot settings, temperature 0, and model configurations are unchanged. Appendix H retains the same BERT training/validation design, training budget, and hyperparameters.

E4.justification: Both retain the explanation, single-stage, and persuasion-knowledge ablations, persuasion correlations and subset analyses, and unseen-data BERT comparison. Sections 4–6 and Appendices E, G, and H contain no added or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Standard-deviation reporting across models or prompting methods and the McNemar significance analysis remain unchanged, including Table 18. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 5 retains average F1 scores of 0.711 for Base and 0.815 for PCoT; Tables 24–25 retain BERT's 0.485. No result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same formal inputs, outputs, and Equations (1)–(3). No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same PCoT contribution, two dataset contributions, and claimed average 15% improvement. Novelty and applicability claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of longer-text gains, persuasion correlations, and difficulties without persuasion remain identical. The English-only evaluation, dataset and annotation biases, fixed taxonomy, and inability to isolate individual strategies retain the same qualifications.

D1.justification: Annotation and preprocessing details, prompt descriptions, model/API specifications, BERT hyperparameters and hardware, and code/data links are unchanged. The stated dataset license remains CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

R1.justification: Section 7 and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. No prior-work comparisons or novelty relationships are added, removed, or revised.

P1.justification: The arXiv stamp updates from v1, 7 June 2025, to v2, 8 January 2026. PDF document-license metadata changes from CC BY 4.0 to CC BY-SA 4.0. Body wording, headings, and section/appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All 12 figures and 25 tables retain their content, captions, structure, color coding, and placement. Rendered pages preserve the same layout; extraction-spacing and negligible rendering differences do not establish a presentation revision.

improvement.justification: The main text and appendices preserve the same method, empirical evidence, statistical analyses, reproducibility information, limitations, and presentation. The administrative stamp and document-metadata updates do not establish a meaningful improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
